protocol.description:
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.
This protocol allows a privileged DDE client such as the dock to monitor whether a region anchored to an edge of an output overlaps with any xdg-shell toplevel window, for example to implement smart panel hiding.
The compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

interface.name: treeland_window_overlap_checker_manager_v1
interface.description:
A global that creates treeland_window_overlap_checker_v1 objects for privileged DDE clients. Each checker monitors one region; clients monitoring several regions create several checkers.
The compositor must reject bind attempts from non-privileged clients.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_window_overlap_checker_manager_v1 object. Checkers created through this manager are not affected.

request.name: get_window_overlap_checker
request.description: Create a new treeland_window_overlap_checker_v1 object that monitors one region.

interface.name: treeland_window_overlap_checker_v1

description.summary: overlap monitor for an edge-anchored region

interface.description:
A checker object monitors whether a rectangular region anchored to an edge of an output overlaps with any xdg-shell toplevel window.
The client registers the monitored region with the set_region request and the compositor reports transitions between the overlapped and clear states with the enter and leave events. The recorded region only changes when set_region is called; the client must call set_region again whenever the monitored panel moves or resizes.
After each set_region request the compositor should evaluate the region against the current window layout and send the matching enter or leave event; afterwards it should send these events only when the overlap state changes.
The checker is associated with the wl_output passed to the last set_region request. When that output is destroyed the compositor sends the output_removed event; the checker then becomes inert: it has no monitored region and sends no further enter or leave events. The checker object itself is not destroyed by output removal; the client may call set_region again with another wl_output to resume monitoring, or call destroy to release it. The compositor must not send enter, leave, or output_removed after output_removed until the next successful set_region.

enum.name: anchor

description.summary: output edge the region is anchored to

enum.description: The registered region is a strip along the anchored edge of the output: for top and bottom the strip spans the full output width and is height units thick; for left and right it spans the full output height and is width units thick.

entry.name: top
entry.summary: strip along the top edge of the output

entry.name: bottom
entry.summary: strip along the bottom edge of the output

entry.name: left
entry.summary: strip along the left edge of the output

entry.name: right
entry.summary: strip along the right edge of the output

enum.name: error
enum.description: Errors raised by the treeland_window_overlap_checker_v1 interface.

entry.name: invalid_anchor
entry.summary: anchor is not one of the enum values

entry.name: invalid_size
entry.summary: width or height is not positive

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the treeland_window_overlap_checker_v1 object. The compositor stops monitoring the region registered with this checker.

request.name: set_region
request.description:
Set the monitored region on the given output, or re-register it when the monitored panel moves or resizes. The region geometry is described by the anchor enum; the compositor raises invalid_anchor for an unknown anchor value and invalid_size when width or height is not positive.
The output becomes the output associated with the checker, replacing any previous one; it may be a different output from a previous call (rebinding), for example after the previous output was removed.
After this request the compositor should evaluate the current overlap state and send the matching enter or leave event.

arg.name: anchor
arg.summary: output edge the region is anchored to

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output whose edge anchors the region

event.name: enter
event.description: Sent when the registered region begins to overlap any xdg-shell toplevel window, and after a set_region request while the region is currently overlapped.

event.name: leave

description.summary: the region is no longer overlapped

event.description: Sent when the registered region stops overlapping all xdg-shell toplevel windows, and after a set_region request while the region is currently clear.

event.name: output_removed

description.summary: the associated output has been destroyed

event.description:
Sent when the wl_output passed to the last set_region request has been destroyed by the compositor. The checker then becomes inert: it has no monitored region and sends no further enter or leave events.
The checker object itself is not destroyed; the client may call set_region again with another wl_output to resume monitoring, or call destroy to release it. The compositor must not send this event more than once without an intervening successful set_region.
